caption: The drawing features three technical views of a gate-leg table made of yellow pine. At the top left, there is a top-down plan view illustrating the oval tabletop, comprised of a central rectangular panel and two rounded drop leaves, with the wood grain and joinery indicated in shades of brown. Below this, two side elevation views show the table's front and side profiles. The table has six turned legs with bulbous forms and multiple cross-stretchers connecting them horizontally. One of the side views depicts the table with the gate legs extended, holding up the drop leaves, while the other shows the leaves in the dropped position. All illustrations are rendered in shades of brown to represent the pine wood. To the right of the top view, hand-written text provides details: "SCALE DRAWING OF GATE-LEG TABLE," specifying yellow pine as the material, Pennsylvania as the place of origin, and a date range of 1700-1725. Additional text identifies the table as being in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, with the accession number 34.100.16 and room L-5. The artist's signature, "A. Rosenfield del.," is written below the description. The drawing is on a light beige background.
title: Gate-leg Table
